Reinsurance premium: the premiums paid less any ceding commission, with the expected reinstatement premiums. Margin: that premium less the expected recoveries. Capital: the mean net result less its 0.5% worst. Value: 10% of the capital relief less the margin, positive when the capital saved is worth more than the reinsurance costs.

How to read this report

  • Rates are shares of the subject premium of the rating year; the expected layer loss is the rate times that premium.
  • Burning cost: each year's losses are brought to the rating year by the claims inflation, put through the layer and developed, over the year's premium brought to the rating year's rate level.
  • Pareto: the losses above the Pareto threshold, in the money of the rating year, give the expected number of losses and, from the Pareto's alpha, the share of each that falls in the layer.
  • Exposure: each band of the risk profile gives its expected loss to the layer, from an exposure curve (property) or the limited expected values of a claim size distribution (casualty).
  • The technical premium is the blended expected loss over one minus the loading, split between the upfront premium and the expected reinstatement premiums. The rate on line is the upfront premium over the limit, and the payback its inverse, in years.
  • Programmes: the capital is the mean net result less its result in the bad year of the level chosen; the value of a programme is the cost of the capital it saves less the margin it pays the reinsurers.
